intro: にかけて marks the far end of a stretch whose edges are soft: 'from around A through to around B'. The image is something spread across a span of time or space, like weather moving over a region, rather than a clean start and stop. It is the language of forecasts, seasons and maps.

skills.rule: A から B にかけて: across the span from A to B, with loose edges; B is an end point, not a length.
skills.explain:
Put an end point after にかけて, usually with a starting point and から before it: 今夜から明日にかけて雨が降る (rain from tonight into tomorrow), 関東から東北にかけて (from Kanto across to Tohoku), 首から肩にかけて痛い (it hurts from my neck down to my shoulders). It suits broad points: times of day, days, months, seasons, regions, parts of the body. The event fills the stretch, but nobody is promising the exact moment it starts or stops.

It can stand without から: 週末にかけて晴れる (fine weather into the weekend).

The edge: まで gives a sharp end point (五時まで働く), and までに is a deadline (金曜日までに出す). にかけて never follows a length such as 三日間 or 十年; a length takes にわたって. を通して means without a break through a whole period. Separately, Xにかけては means 'when it comes to X' (料理にかけては), which is a different use.
patterns: [A] から [B] にかけて [event spread over the span]
[B] にかけて [event continuing into B]

examples.jp: 今夜[こんや]から明日[あした]{にかけて}雨[あめ]が降[ふ]るでしょう。
examples.en: It will probably rain from tonight into tomorrow.

examples.jp: 三月[さんがつ]から四月[しがつ]{にかけて}桜[さくら]が咲[さ]きます。
examples.en: The cherry trees bloom from March into April.

examples.jp: 年末[ねんまつ]から年始[ねんし]{にかけて}、実家[じっか]で過[す]ごします。
examples.en: I'll spend the New Year period at my parents' home.

examples.jp: 首[くび]から肩[かた]{にかけて}痛[いた]みがあります。
examples.en: I have pain from my neck down to my shoulders.

examples.jp: 関東[かんとう]から東北[とうほく]{にかけて}大雪[おおゆき]になりました。
examples.en: There was heavy snow from the Kanto region across to Tohoku.

contrast.note: 九時から五時まで働く gives exact limits. にかけて gives a rough stretch, as in a forecast or a season.
までに is a deadline: something happens once, at or before B. にかけて describes something that fills the span.
にわたって follows a length or extent: 三日間にわたって, 全国にわたって. にかけて follows an end point: 明日にかけて.

mistakes.bad: 会議[かいぎ]は三日間[みっかかん]{にかけて}行[おこな]われた。
mistakes.good: 会議[かいぎ]は三日間[みっかかん]{にわたって}行[おこな]われた。
mistakes.note: 三日間 is a length, not an end point, so にわたって.

mistakes.bad: 金曜日[きんようび]{にかけて}レポートを出[だ]してください。
mistakes.good: 金曜日[きんようび]{までに}レポートを出[だ]してください。
mistakes.note: Handing something in is a one-off act with a deadline: までに.

skills.tip: Point at the word before the blank: is it a place on the calendar or map where a rough stretch ends? にかけて. A length → にわたって. A deadline → までに.
